summary: Lava and water are completely transparent at certain height levels
description:
## The bug

When standing so that the player is just inside lava (a very small range), it is possible to see through it (third screenshot). This also occurs when the player's head is back against a block and touching a block above it in flowing lava that is next to a source block (first two screenshots).

## How to reproduce

## No surface and no tint

 - Switch to Creative mode and start flying

 - Use the following commands

/setblock ~ 64 ~ lava

/tp ~ 62.39 ~

 - Start looking up and down

→ At some point you will see no bottom surface but also no tint

## Surface and tint

 - Switch to Creative mode and start flying

 - Use the following commands

/setblock ~ 64 ~ water

/tp ~ 63.39 ~

 - Start looking up and down

→ At some point you will see the top surface and the tint
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Switch to Creative mode.
2. Start flying.
3. Execute `/setblock ~ 64 ~ lava`.
4. Execute `/tp ~ 62.39 ~`.
5. Look up and down.
6. Observe that, at some point, the lava has no visible bottom surface and provides no tint.
7. Execute `/setblock ~ 64 ~ water`.
8. Execute `/tp ~ 63.39 ~`.
9. Look up and down.
10. Observe that, at some point, the water's top surface and tint are visible.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.4.4, 1.4.5, 1.4.7, 1.5, 1.6.2, 1.7.4, 14w08a, 1.7.5, 14w10c, 14w11b, 1.7.9, 14w17a, 14w18b, 14w19a, 14w20a, 14w20b, 14w21b, 1.10.2, 16w32a, 16w32b, 16w33a, 16w35a, 1.11.1, 18w07c, 1.13-pre6, 1.14.2, 1.15.2, 20w06a, 20w08a, 20w22a, 1.16 Pre-release 3, 1.16 Pre-release 4, 1.16 Release Candidate 1, 1.16, 1.16.1, 20w27a, 20w28a, 20w30a, 1.16.2 Pre-release 1, 1.16.2 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3, 1.16.4 Pre-release 1, 1.16.4 Pre-release 2, 1.16.4 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.4, 20w45a, 20w46a (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
## Actual behavior

When the player’s camera is positioned within a narrow vertical range inside a lava block, the liquid is not rendered correctly. The lava surface and the underwater-style color tint disappear, allowing the player to see through the lava as if the block were transparent. Looking up or down can move the camera into or out of this rendering state.

The same issue can occur in flowing lava next to a lava source when the player’s head is pressed against a nearby block and the block above it. In the corresponding water setup, changing the player’s view can also cause the fluid surface and tint to appear or disappear depending on the camera’s height and orientation.
Expected Behavior: Lava and water should remain visibly rendered when the player’s viewpoint is partially inside them, regardless of the player’s exact height or position. Lava should retain its surface and characteristic tint, while water should retain its surface and underwater tint. Looking up or down, including near blocks or flowing water and lava beside source blocks, should not make either fluid completely transparent.
